title: 2023 AMC 12A Problem 23
statement: How many ordered pairs of positive real numbers \((a,b)\) satisfy the equation \[ \begin{gathered} (1+2a)(2+2b)(2a+b)\\ {}=32ab? \end{gathered} \]

solutions.text:
By AM-GM, \(1+2a\ge 2\sqrt{2a},\) \(2+2b\ge 4\sqrt{b},\) and \(2a+b\ge 2\sqrt{2ab}.\) Multiplying, \[ \begin{gathered} (1+2a)(2+2b)(2a+b)\\ {}\ge 16\sqrt{2a}\cdot\sqrt{b}\cdot\sqrt{2ab}\\ {}=32ab. \end{gathered} \]

Equality requires \(1=2a,\) \(2=2b,\) and \(2a=b\) simultaneously. These give \(a=\tfrac12,\) \(b=1,\) which are consistent, so there is exactly one solution.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The product is at least \(32ab,\) so equality must hold in all three inequalities at once
